concerns.location: tasks.md:Execution order (T006, T007, T008 parallel claim)
concerns.text: Execution order states 'T006/T007/T008 touch distinct outputs and may run in parallel after T005', but T007 and T008 BOTH implement code in `code/modeling/evaluate.py' ('In code/modeling/evaluate.py' appears in both), and T006 wraps 'training/evaluation' with the memory profiler — i.e., it also modifies the evaluation path. Three tasks concurrently editing the same module is not parallel-safe; either serialize them or split evaluate.py work into distinct files/functions before granting parallelism.

T001 is tagged [P] but is the first task in the list with nothing to run alongside; harmless, though its second bullet (confirming config.py constants and documenting quickstart.md) touches docs that T003's orchestration and T012's quickstart-based re-run depend on — fine as ordered, but the [P] tag adds no value and could invite concurrent edits to quickstart.md.
